analyst_view.overall: Early view: the north London derby with Arsenal top on 27 points, seven clean sheets and 444 league minutes without conceding, against a Spurs side that lost at Leeds and has a long attacking injury list. Spurs play Fulham on Thursday, Arsenal at Brentford on Wednesday, and Arsenal have Champions League football the following week. Arsenal's 1-0 habit and a derby edge point to a tight, physical game.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. I lean lower: Arsenal have won 34 league games 1-0 under Mikel Arteta and concede almost nothing, while Spurs are missing Xavi Simons, Wilson Odobert and others and only scored 10 in 10. A low-scoring Arsenal win fits best.

corners.text: The site has 10.7 corners. I agree: Arsenal earn plenty of corners and are dangerous from them, and Spurs will push forward at home. No clear reason to move.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.7 cards. I agree: it is a derby, Pedro Porro and Roberto De Zerbi were both booked at Leeds, and Arsenal are happy to slow games down when ahead. Five or six bookings is in line with the figure.

shots.text: The site has 25.2 shots. I lean lower: Arsenal held Liverpool to no shots on target at Anfield and limit teams well, and Spurs' attacking injuries cut their options. Fewer shots than the figure.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.6 shots on target. I lean lower: Arsenal's defence allows very few clean chances and their own attack, without Bukayo Saka, has been wasteful. Six on target looks more likely.
